# Admissibility — which offset patterns can repeat forever

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [Patterns, admissibility and the Hardy-Littlewood constants](../../GRAPH.md#patterns-admissibility-and-the-hardy-littlewood-constants)

An offset pattern only has to be checked at the wheels no larger than the number of offsets; the pattern {0, 2, 4} fails at the wheel of size 3; an evenly spaced run passes exactly when every wheel up to its length divides the spacing (the Lagrange–Waring condition).

## Claims

<a id="admissible_of_large_primes"></a>
### `admissible_of_large_primes`

Admissibility only needs checking at wheels no larger than the number of offsets.

```lean
/-- **Only the small wheels need checking.** If no wheel no larger than the
number of offsets is completely covered, the pattern is admissible: a larger
wheel has more positions than the pattern has offsets, so it can never be
covered. -/
def admissible_of_large_primes : Prop :=
  ∀ T : Finset Nat, (∀ p, p.Prime → p ≤ T.card → w T p < p) → is_admissible T
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.Admissibility.admissible_of_large_primes_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/Admissibility.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Admissibility.lean)

<a id="zero_two_admissible"></a>
### `zero_two_admissible`

The twin pattern {0, 2} is admissible.

```lean
/-- **The twin pattern is admissible.** The offsets {0, 2} never cover every
position of any wheel. -/
def zero_two_admissible : Prop :=
  is_admissible ({0, 2} : Finset Nat)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.Admissibility.zero_two_admissible_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/Admissibility.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Admissibility.lean)

<a id="zero_two_four_not_admissible"></a>
### `zero_two_four_not_admissible`

The pattern {0, 2, 4} covers every position of the wheel of size 3.

```lean
/-- **The pattern {0, 2, 4} is not admissible.** It covers all three
positions of the wheel of size 3, so one of any three such numbers is always
a multiple of 3. -/
def zero_two_four_not_admissible : Prop :=
  ¬ is_admissible ({0, 2, 4} : Finset Nat)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.Admissibility.zero_two_four_not_admissible_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/Admissibility.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Admissibility.lean)

<a id="ap_offsets_admissible_iff"></a>
### `ap_offsets_admissible_iff`

An evenly spaced run is admissible exactly when every prime up to its length divides the spacing (Lagrange-Waring).

```lean
/-- **The Lagrange–Waring condition.** For a nonzero spacing, the pattern of
an evenly spaced run passes the admissibility test exactly when every prime
no larger than the run length divides the spacing. -/
def ap_offsets_admissible_iff : Prop :=
  ∀ d k : Nat, d ≠ 0 →
    (is_admissible (ap_offsets d k) ↔ ∀ p, p.Prime → p ≤ k → p ∣ d)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.Admissibility.ap_offsets_admissible_iff_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/Admissibility.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Admissibility.lean)
